name: org.machanism.machai:genai-client
description: GenAI Client is a Java library for integrating Machai applications with generative AI providers through a stable provider abstraction. It supports provider resolution, prompt and instruction handling, conversational generation, function tool registration, prompt and resource annotations, embedding generation, usage statistics, input logging, optional web search, and MCP server configuration. Concrete adapters include OpenAI-compatible providers, Anthropic Claude providers, CodeMie OAuth 2.0 delegation, and a deterministic YAML ToolsProvider for local tool-only workflows. It is useful for semantic search, similarity comparison, automated content generation, intelligent project assembly, model-assisted workflows, tool-enabled agents, and provider-agnostic AI application development in the Machanism ecosystem.

usageContext: Java applications that need a provider-neutral GenAI API
Applications that call OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic Claude models
CodeMie-backed AI applications that authenticate through OAuth 2.0
Agentic workflows that expose Java methods as AI-callable tools
Semantic search and similarity workflows that require embedding vectors
Applications that need token usage tracking and model usage reporting
Tool-only automation workflows that invoke local Java functions from YAML

constructors.description: Creates an OpenAI-compatible Genai provider. Initialize it with org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.impl.OpenAIProvider.init(java.lang.String, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator) before use. Configuration keys include OPENAI_API_KEY, optional OPENAI_BASE_URL, GENAI_TIMEOUT, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, MAX_TOOL_CALLS, WebSearchTool.* values, and MCP.* groups.

examples.description: Instantiates and configures the OpenAI provider, sends instructions and a user prompt, executes generation, and clears accumulated conversation state. The configurator must supply OPENAI_API_KEY and may supply OPENAI_BASE_URL for OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

constructors.description: Creates an Anthropic Claude Genai provider. Initialize it with a Claude model and a configurator containing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and optional ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, GENAI_TIMEOUT, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, MAX_TOOL_CALLS, web search, and MCP settings.

examples.description: Creates and runs an Anthropic-backed provider. Use this when a Machai application needs Claude message generation, local function tools, optional web search, or MCP server forwarding.

constructors.description: Creates a CodeMie provider that obtains an OAuth 2.0 token from CodeMie and delegates to OpenAIProvider or AnthropicProvider based on the model prefix. Required configuration keys are GENAI_USERNAME and GENAI_PASSWORD; AUTH_URL may override the token endpoint.

examples.description: Authenticates to CodeMie and delegates the request to an OpenAI-compatible backend for a GPT-style model. For Claude-prefixed models, delegation is routed to the Anthropic provider.

constructors.description: Creates a deterministic local tool provider. When initialized with the model name yaml, the last submitted prompt is parsed as a YAML tool-call descriptor and the matching registered tool is invoked. The provider disables conversational error handling and propagates tool failures in fail-fast mode.

examples.description: Configures a local tool-only workflow. Register tools through a FunctionTools implementation, submit YAML that names the tool and parameters, and call perform to execute the local function.

features.name: getProvider
features.signature: public static org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.Genai getProvider(java.lang.String chatModel, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator conf)
features.description: Dynamically loads and initializes a Genai chat provider from a Provider:Model string. Provider names without a package are resolved using org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.impl.{Provider}Provider. Fully qualified provider class names are supported when the provider segment contains a dot. Returns null when the provider name is blank and throws java.lang.IllegalArgumentException when resolution or initialization fails.

examples.description: Resolves a provider by configuration string and runs a chat request without hard-coding the concrete provider class in application code.

features.name: getEmbeddingProvider
features.description: Dynamically loads and initializes an EmbeddingProvider from a Provider:Model string. The resolved provider must implement org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.EmbeddingProvider. Use it to generate embedding vectors for semantic search, similarity comparison, or retrieval workflows.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.EmbeddingProvider embedder = org.machanism.machai.ai.manager.GenaiProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider("OpenAI:text-embedding-3-small", configurator);
java.util.List<java.lang.Double> vector = embedder.embedding("GenAI provider abstraction for Java applications", 1536L);
examples.description: Creates an embedding provider and produces a vector for text that can be indexed for semantic retrieval.

features.name: addTools
features.description: Registers Java methods annotated with org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.Tool from a FunctionTools instance as AI-callable function tools. AbstractAIProvider inspects public methods, extracts tool names and descriptions, converts parameter metadata, and registers callbacks for provider-specific execution.

examples.description: Adds host-defined Java capabilities to a model run so the model can request function calls during generation.

features.name: perform
features.description: Executes the provider using accumulated prompts, instructions, files, and registered tools. OpenAIProvider and AnthropicProvider process tool-call loops until final text is produced. ToolsProvider executes a local tool described by YAML when configured with the yaml model.

examples.description: Runs a generation request and then clears the provider session so the same instance can be reused for another independent request.

features.name: addUsage
features.signature: public static void addUsage(java.lang.String modelId, org.machanism.machai.ai.manager.Usage usage)
features.description: Adds a token-usage record for a model identifier. UsageStatistics groups entries by model and exposes methods to query or log aggregated usage across requests.

examples.description: Records and logs token usage for operational monitoring, cost visibility, or diagnostics.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.FunctionTools
customizations.description: Service-provider interface for bundling host-provided tools, prompts, and resources. Implementations can be discovered with java.util.ServiceLoader and registered with providers by FunctionToolsLoader. Annotate public methods with Tool, Prompt, Resource, and Param to expose structured capabilities.

examples.description: Defines a custom FunctionTools implementation with a tool method that can be registered on a Genai provider.

customizations.name: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GENAI_USERNAME, GENAI_PASSWORD, OPENAI_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, GENAI_TIMEOUT, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, MAX_TOOL_CALLS, WebSearchTool.*, MCP.*
customizations.description: Configuration properties consumed by concrete providers. API key and base URL values configure OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic clients. GENAI_USERNAME and GENAI_PASSWORD configure CodeMie token retrieval. WebSearchTool.* enables provider web search, while MCP.*, MCP_1.*, MCP_2.*, and subsequent groups register MCP server tools until no URL is found.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.Genai
studs.description: Primary contract for generative AI provider integrations. It defines initialization, prompting, clearing state, instructions, response generation, input logging, tool registration, prompt registration, resource registration, project directory configuration, error handling, and enabled tool selection.

examples.description: Uses the Genai interface rather than a concrete class so applications can switch providers through configuration.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.EmbeddingProvider
studs.description: Contract for providers that initialize with model configuration and return embedding vectors for input text. Implemented by OpenAIProvider and CodeMieProvider for semantic search and similarity workflows.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.EmbeddingProvider provider = org.machanism.machai.ai.manager.GenaiProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider("CodeMie:text-embedding-005", configurator);
java.util.List<java.lang.Double> embedding = provider.embedding("searchable content", 768L);
examples.description: Uses an embedding provider to generate vectors for a retrieval index.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.AbstractAIProvider
studs.description: Base implementation of the Genai contract shared by concrete providers. It centralizes configuration, request input logging, tool invocation safety, MCP and web-search bootstrap logic, annotation-driven tools, prompts, resources, project directory propagation, timeout handling, and configurable error-handling behavior.

examples.title: Install the library in a Maven project
steps: Add the genai-client dependency to your Maven pom.xml.
Provide an SLF4J implementation at runtime if your application needs logging output.
Configure provider credentials through your application configurator or environment-backed configuration source.
examples.description: Installs GenAI Client as a Maven dependency. For snapshot versions, ensure that the Sonatype Central snapshots repository is available in your Maven settings or project repository configuration.

examples.title: Configure and run an OpenAI-compatible chat provider
steps: Store OPENAI_API_KEY in the Configurator used by the application.
Optionally set OPENAI_BASE_URL for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and GENAI_TIMEOUT for request timeouts.
Resolve the provider with GenaiProviderManager.getProvider using the OpenAI:Model format.
Submit instructions and prompts, then call perform.
examples.description: A practical end-to-end scenario for using the library in an application service that needs provider-agnostic text generation.

examples.title: Configure CodeMie delegation for enterprise AI access
steps: Configure GENAI_USERNAME and GENAI_PASSWORD in the Configurator.
Optionally configure AUTH_URL when the default CodeMie token endpoint is not suitable.
Use CodeMie:gpt-* for OpenAI-compatible delegation or CodeMie:claude-* for Anthropic delegation.
Run the request through the common Genai interface.
examples.description: Shows how to use CodeMie authentication while keeping application code independent of the downstream provider implementation.

examples.title: Run a local YAML tool invocation with ToolsProvider
steps: Create a FunctionTools implementation with methods annotated by org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.Tool.
Instantiate ToolsProvider and initialize it with model yaml.
Register the FunctionTools instance using addTools.
Submit YAML containing the tool name and params object.
Call perform to execute the local Java function.
examples.description: Demonstrates a deterministic tool-only scenario useful for automation, testing, or workflows where the last prompt should directly execute a local registered Java tool.

examples.title: Generate embeddings for semantic search
steps: Choose an embedding model string such as OpenAI:text-embedding-3-small or CodeMie:text-embedding-005.
Resolve an EmbeddingProvider with GenaiProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider.
Call embedding with the text to index and the desired provider-specific dimensionality.
Store the returned java.util.List<java.lang.Double> in a vector index or compare it with other vectors.
examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.ai.provider.EmbeddingProvider provider = org.machanism.machai.ai.manager.GenaiProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider("OpenAI:text-embedding-3-small", configurator);
java.util.List<java.lang.Double> vector = provider.embedding("Machai provider abstraction and tool calling", 1536L);
examples.description: Practical embedding workflow for semantic search, similarity comparison, retrieval augmented generation, or content clustering.
